why: Rule 1 at the only deg-4 junction: 2 of 4 prongs rise away and none toward, the mu/p chain climbs monotonically 18k->195k over 20 cm to the Bragg stop at 19001, and two more prongs drop to 14-16k at 19005; competitor 80043 sits at the z=1 wall with only flat adjacent segments.

Rule 1, 2 of 2 rising away at the only junction in the event: the 54 cm mu climbs the muon template to 160k at 14002 and the 51 cm p falls from 325k at 14000, so both arms Bragg-terminate at their far ends, which one scattered particle cannot do; prong angle 142 deg, below the collinearity screen.

No rise-away anywhere and the principal frame shows clusters 53/56/54/55 on one straight through-going MIP line, so their deg-2/3 points are fit breaks; picked the cool end of cluster 11, the only >MIP object (40k rising through 110k to 210k = stopping proton), but it is deg 1 and isolated, so it may be a neutron recoil.

Rule 1: 9003 is the only vertex with a prong rising away, the 9.7 cm segment runs 45k MIP from it and spikes to 232k in the last 1.3 cm at 9001, so 9001 is the stop and the track starts at 9003, which sits in a knot of very-low-charge dust; 9000 only 2 cm off keeps it off certain.

Rule 1, 2 of 2 rising away at a sharp kink: the pi+ climbs the proton template to 230k at 21001 and the 176 cm muon ends at 21000, which carries a 6 cm Michel 1.9 cm away (rule 3 makes that the far end); charge also spikes to ~155k in the first bin of both prongs, an unresolved recoil at the vertex.

Rule 1 plus dE/dx vs residual range: 7003->7000 climbs 55k->105k->230k over 37 cm as a stopping proton while the other arm is flat 50-60k MIP for 90 cm out to the x+ wall, which no single particle can do (a proton 127 cm from its stop would be ~33k), and charge jumps 53k->78k across the junction.

The collinearity trap fires on 7002 (prongs 179.4 deg apart, so it is a fit break inside one 125 cm track); p4 shows a textbook stopping-muon Bragg at 7000, so the muon starts at the other end 7001, which carries a 325k point and sits at the edge of the fragment cloud including cluster 49 only 3.8 cm away.

Nothing converges in this event; cluster 80 zooms as one continuous bent 22 cm track with a steep 200k Bragg stop at 80031, so its cool 53k free end 80030 is that proton's start, but 6001 is a 28.8 deg shower hairpin, cluster 35 is an isolated 208k stub, and 80034 is 9 cm away.

Rule 1 at a deg-3 junction, 2 of 3 rising away and none toward: a 13 cm proton climbs the template 123k->190k to its stop at 8005, and the 76.7 cm muon runs MIP then peaks 152k at 8003 with a 14 cm MIP Michel continuing past it, which by rule 3 makes 8003 the far end; angles 81/134/145 deg.

Rule 1: seg 19002 is a textbook stopping muon, MIP for 85 cm then up the template to 140k at 19001, so the 100 cm muon starts at 19002, and both its ends are interior; the zoom shows a 108 deg kink with a sharp cyan-to-orange charge break (45k vs 85k) meaning two particles, though 19003 23 cm away also holds a stopping proton.

Both arms ride the proton template to Bragg stops at their far ends (258k at 7000, 265k at 7003, falling to ~118k at 7004), and one particle can only stop once, so 7004 is a real 2 of 2 rise-away junction; dropped one tier because the prongs leave at 172.5 deg, firing the collinearity screen.

The two long arms are exactly 180 deg apart, so they are one straight 175 cm track running from the x- wall to 7 cm off the y- wall with no Bragg at either end, and the 14 cm branch at 16002 is flat MIP, reading as a delta ray; the dust sits 5-18 cm off that track, so no vertex topology exists and this is only the least-bad point.

The event is one 67.7 cm segment with deg-1 ends plus four dots lying 20-42 cm off it, and p4 is flat ~90k across with no Bragg at either end; rule 1 (67k vs 92k) and rule 2 both favour 13001, which I kept despite it touching the x+ anode face because the wall rule forbids screening it out.

Rule 1 on the event's dominant object: seg 9000 runs flat 45-55k MIP for 11.5 cm then rises 56k->93k->140k in the last 2 cm at 9001, so 9001 is the stop and the cool end 9000 is the start; no junction exists anywhere and rule 2 mildly disagrees, so not certain.
